copy.plan_purpose: The whole plan: shared types at the root, eight crates in three lanes that build on them, one integration story that assembles the crates, and an external gate that releases the result.
copy.plan_relations: Identity check and pg-core build directly on the shared types, and six more crates build on pg-core; Bootstrap takes one input from each of the eight crates, and the external gate needs Bootstrap alone.

m0.purpose: the shared type surface and port contract every other crate programs against

laneA.purpose: the lane that lands the core rules and the check that re-verifies them

laneB.purpose: the lane that closes contracts and turns them into compiled artifacts

laneC.purpose: the lane that records proof: evidence, the ledger, admission, and planning control

gates.purpose: the assembly and external gates that turn finished crates into a shipped product

M0.role: defines the shared types and byte formats every crate builds against
M0.makes: the shared type and byte contract

IIC.role: recomputes content identity on its own, to catch pg-core if it is wrong

CORE.role: turns raw bytes into canonical bytes, content IDs and verified signers
CORE.makes: canonical bytes, content IDs and verified signers

CONT.role: closes typed records into checked contract sets

COMP.role: turns what an author intends into closed contracts or open questions

EVID.role: captures evidence against one frozen candidate and stores it by content

LEDG.role: stores authority records durably, one transaction at a time

ADMT.role: decides whether a request is allowed under current authority

PLCT.role: is the command line that sends each command to the right crate

BOOT.role: assembles all eight crates into one workspace once each has landed

S7.role: is the external release gate after integration

M0-IIC.meaning: the type and byte contract it recomputes identity against

M0-CORE.meaning: the types, port traits and error shapes it must implement exactly

CORE-CONT.meaning: canonical bytes, content IDs and verified signers

CORE-EVID.meaning: the frozen candidate each evidence record points at

CORE-LEDG.meaning: validated transitions to append as authority records

CORE-ADMT.meaning: the authority state each admission decision reads

CORE-PLCT.meaning: the core rules behind each routed command

CONT-COMP.meaning: closed contract sets and selector rules

CONT-EVID.meaning: the conformance claims evidence must cover

CONT-ADMT.meaning: the contracts each admitted delta must satisfy

CONT-PLCT.meaning: contract status used to sequence work

ADMT-PLCT.meaning: the gate each planned command passes through

EVID-PLCT.meaning: proof records that mark work done

CORE-BOOT.meaning: the validated core the workspace links in

CONT-BOOT.meaning: the closed contracts the build satisfies

ADMT-BOOT.meaning: the admission decision on the assembled product

BOOT-S7.meaning: the assembled product the gate receives
